1The city screen, simpler

You said: "this is too cluttered, could you make it a bit simpler and less overwhelming for new players? The build list doesn't require icons… The bottom bar feels too busy."

A new player needs three answers at a glance: what the town is building, how it grows, and what it can build next. The screen now shows those and folds the rest. One version only.

What stays in viewThe build list, exactly as today: the gear, the cost, the turns, the price. On the left, three segments: growth, borders, and the citizens' focus.
What is foldedOne row each, with a count: Buildings, Great houses, Wonders, Specialists, Faith, Levy a citizen. A row opens in place, and one row is open at a time. A row with nothing in it is not drawn.
What I removed, and where it wentThe band at the foot: gone; its three lists are fold rows. The treasury and faith in the head: gone; the build list says "you have 555 gold", and the Faith row holds the faith. The Supply line: into the list's Units tab, where it matters. "Next citizen 18 / 128" and "Next hex": on hover of each meter. The Dismiss buttons: in the Specialists row. The levy menu: opens from its row, as today's menu.

Cost to build: medium. The left panel is new; the build list is not touched except for the Supply line. The fold rows are the height guard too: the panel is about 330 px at rest, so it fits a 700 px window.

2Diplomacy, layout B

You said: "I like this one better actually. What happens if you click standing and deals? Also, i'm worried there wont be enough room on the top bar for all portraits."

Two answers. First, "Standing and deals" is one button today and it opens one drawer; I kept that. Second, two ways to change court that hold eleven other seats.

Standing and dealsToday the drawer holds: the relation and the two border lines; the deals in force with their turns left; papers that wait for your answer (Read); your own offers (Withdraw); and the other acts (peace, Declare war). In B the drawer slides over the right side. The portrait and the words stay in view. The × or Esc goes back to the exchange. The button shows the count of deals, and a dot when a paper waits. Declare war is not in the drawer now: it is the button at the foot.
Changing court: the strip (recommended)A column of charges down the left edge of the portrait, 30 px each. Eleven fit in the portrait's height. A dot marks a war or a waiting paper. A court you have not met is faint. The name shows on hover. One click changes court, and the up and down keys do the same.
Changing court: the nameplateThe name on the portrait is the control: arrows step to the next court, and a click on the name opens a list of all of them. It is the cleanest at rest, but it hides who else is there, and a far court costs two clicks.

I recommend the strip. You see every court and its state without a click, and the head of the sheet stays empty. It uses charges, not faces, so it needs no small portraits. Splash art slot: the leader portrait, 3:4, about 318 by 424 px; fallback the seat's charge.

Cost to build: medium. The trays and the paper keep today's logic. The drawer exists; it moves. The strip is new.

3Faith: the tab order, and Religion & followers

You said: "lets move bonuses to the third tab. Could we have a reworked version of the religion and followers tab too? it looks quite dated."

The tabs are now Rites, Religion & followers, Bonuses. Rites opens first for a seat that has not chosen a tab; after that the sheet opens on the tab the player last used, as it does today.

What changedThe page is two plain tables and one short list, in the style of the Rites page. The four boxes become one line. Rival pressure becomes a column, so one row tells the whole state of a town. A new small table lists the religions in the world with founder, holy city and towns. The clergy become rows.
Splash art slotNone on this page. The pantheon wheel is its picture.

Cost to build: small to medium. The "Religions in the world" table shows one new fact (the towns of each religion); check that the rules can count it for a rival.

Every fact of today's page, and where it is now:

  • The religion's name, and the control to rename it: in the head.
  • "Founded by you" and the holy city: in the head.
  • "1 of 2 religions founded": the foot of the "Religions in the world" table.

4The Order draft offer

You said: "The text below the card isn't needed. Lets make sure this is basically the same as the great people draft screen, just with order cards. There feels like too much negative space on the bottom. Make sure to preserve the animations, maybe adding a flipping effect here and have the cards reveal themselves one by one?"

It is now the great person sheet with Order cards: the same head, the same place for "Ask again" at the left and the choice at the right, and Pass beside the choice. The line under each card is gone. The sheet is as tall as its content.

What changedNo text under the cards. The sheet is 444 px tall, not 532. The card's foot shows the flourish until the pick, because today's figure arrives on the pick.
The revealKeep today's flip and slow the gap between cards from 110 to 260 ms, after a 300 ms hold on the three backs. The whole reveal is 1240 ms; today it is 640 ms. The back is the draft pile's back.
Skip, and reduced motionA click or a key during the reveal turns every card up at once and chooses nothing. With reduced motion the cards are face up from the start and the figure appears without a count.

The great person offer should get the same reveal. It is the same sheet in the code (src/ui/offerCard.ts), and so is the charter. One change of two numbers covers all three, and three offers that behave alike are easier to learn.

Cost to build: small. The card face and the deal exist. New: the hold, the longer gap, and the skip.

Today's animations, all kept:

  • The sheet arrives: the ground fades in 160 ms and the sheet settles in 240 ms.
  • The deal: each card is laid face down and turns over in 420 ms, one 110 ms after the other (src/ui/cardDeal.ts). So the flip exists today; it is too quick to read as "one by one".
  • The stamp on the pick: a card shows a flourish while it is a choice. When it is taken, its figure counts up over about 750 ms, lands (420 ms) and glows (520 ms). This is "the number arrives on the pick" (src/ui/cardStamp.ts).
  • The leave: the taken card holds while the others fall away, and the sheet goes at 1450 ms.
  • Reduced motion: no deal at all; the cards are drawn face up.

6The unit panel, with the forecast at the bottom left

You said: "lets make sure this forecast is on the bottom left, where it used to be."

Done. In the game the forecast is the first block of the hex card at the bottom left (#combat-forecast, inside the card that shows terrain and yields). The frame puts it there and follows the real block part for part.

The real forecast's partsA head ("Shoot" or "Attack" and the name). Two columns: each side's name, its strength as a large figure, and the lines that make it. Two rows: each side's damage with its spread ("−41 ±5"), a health bar with the loss marked, and the health after. Notes replace the columns for a capture, a plunder or a blow that is refused. A dashed frame marks a comparison the unit cannot act on this turn.
What changedNothing in the forecast but the kit: mono figures, the small seal on a line that a card pays. The unit panel at the right is the third pass's: plain buttons in place of teal, Disband apart.

Not captured: I read the forecast from its code (renderCombatForecast in src/main.ts and its CSS), because the game I had was at peace with every unit in reach. The parts above are the real ones; the figures are samples.

7The corner panel: figures that overflow

You said: "i'm noticing in playtesting that these can overflow. Could we slightly lower the text size here and make it so the panel can expand instead of overflowing?"

The figure is the faith count in the corner panel's row of five marks (#quick-faith-figure in .empire-quick, src/style.css). It is not the top bar.

What overflows todayThe panel is fixed at 272 px. The row is five cells: 44, a share, a share, 54 and 44 px. So Routes and Faith get 64 px each. A mark and its gap take 22 px, and the type is 12 px mono, about 7.2 px a character. That leaves room for five characters. While a god has a price, faith reads "banked/price": "120/160" is seven characters and needs 72 px. Routes at "10/12" needs 58 px and just fits. I set these figures in the real game and measured them; the pictures show the result.
The change, for the builderIn .quick-button: the type goes from 12 px to 11 px, the gap from 6 to 4 px, and each cell gets 6 px of padding at each side. In .empire-quick: the two middle columns become as wide as their content and share any room that is left, and the In play column is at least 54 px. In .empire-corner: width becomes min-width of 272 px with the width set by the content. Nothing wraps and nothing is cut.
The resultWith figures of up to five characters the panel stays 272 px. With "120/160" it is about 297 px. With the longest figures the game can print ("1.2k/2.4k", because figures shorten above 999) it is about 310 px. I measured these in the mock-up. The research and draft lines above stretch with the panel.
